source_evidence.observation: The paper defines an s-stage Runge-Kutta method with an s-by-s Butcher array A and a length-s weight vector b. [PDF p. 2, anchor: equation (1.1)]
The perturbation operator is explicitly defined by tau(u) = (F(u) - F_eps(u))/epsilon. [PDF p. 3, anchor: equation (2.3)]
The additive method uses A,b with F and A_eps,b_eps with F_eps, and requires F_eps(y) - F(y) = O(epsilon) for any y. [PDF p. 4, anchor: equations (3.1a)-(3.1b)]

The paper defines tilde_A = A + A_eps and tilde_b = b + b_eps and prints the perturbed representation with positive epsilon A_eps tau and epsilon b_eps tau terms. [PDF p. 5, anchor: equations (3.2a)-(3.2b)]

The one-step error is split as E = E_sch + E_per = O(Delta t^(p+1)) + O(epsilon Delta t^(m+1)); if the method is stable, the stated global form is Error = O(Delta t^p) + O(epsilon Delta t^m). [PDF p. 5, anchor: paragraph following equation (3.3)]

source_evidence.anchor: perturbation expansion table and the two regularity scenarios
source_evidence.observation: The expansion tracks powers through third order in both Delta t and epsilon. In the standard scenario F and F_eps have existing bounded derivatives, so tau and its derivatives are bounded and coefficient cancellations are used. For chopping, F_eps = Chop(F) is described as bounded but not Lipschitz, tau is not Lipschitz, and its derivatives may not exist. [PDF p. 6, anchor: perturbation expansion and regularity discussion]

Consistency through order three requires tilde_b e = 1, tilde_b tilde_c = 1/2, tilde_b(tilde_c componentwise-times tilde_c) = 1/3, and tilde_b tilde_A tilde_c = 1/6. [PDF p. 7, anchor: consistency-order list]

For well-behaved tau, equations (3.5a)-(3.5f) give all cancellation conditions through perturbation order m = 3, grouped by the labels n >= 1, n >= 2, and n >= 3. [PDF p. 8, anchor: equations (3.5a)-(3.5f)]
A worked Butcher-array display explicitly uses tilde_c = c + c_eps together with tilde_A = A + A_eps and tilde_b = b + b_eps. [PDF p. 11, anchor: arrays following equation (4.1c)]

Section 4.3 says Method 4s3pC is devised to satisfy the less restrictive conditions (3.5), which apply only when tau is well-behaved, in contrast with the stricter conditions (3.4). [PDF p. 17, anchor: Section 4.3 opening paragraph]
The paper prints six A entries, ten A_eps entries, four b entries, and b_eps = (0,0,0,0) for Method 4s3pC. [PDF p. 18, anchor: Method 4s3pC coefficient displays]

source_evidence.anchor: two error-form statements following the Method 4s3pC coefficients
source_evidence.observation: The paper explicitly states Error = O(Delta t^3) + O(epsilon Delta t^3) for well-behaved tau and Error = O(Delta t^3) + O(epsilon Delta t^2) when tau is not well-behaved. [PDF p. 18, anchor: error statements following the coefficients]

The centered-difference versus Fourier-spectral difference is identified as well-behaved, whereas chopping the Fourier-spectral evaluation is treated as not well-behaved; the paper also warns that using two different operators requires stability analysis. [PDF p. 19, anchor: discussion of Figure 6]
The paper says epsilon is treated as a single constant upper bound. [PDF p. 20, anchor: final paragraph of Conclusions]

binders: The general framework binds a stage count s, coefficient arrays A,A_eps of size s by s, weight vectors b,b_eps of length s, a step size Delta t, operators F,F_eps, and perturbation scale epsilon. [PDF p. 2, anchor: equation (1.1); PDF p. 4, anchor: equations (3.1a)-(3.1b)]

Method 4s3pC is naturally read as s = 4 because its weights have four entries and its displayed matrix indices range from 1 through 4; that dimension is inferred from the display rather than separately declared in Section 4.3. [PDF p. 18, anchor: Method 4s3pC coefficient displays]

The order parameters are p for consistency order and m for perturbation order; the p = 3, m = 3 smooth case and p = 3, m = 2 nonsmooth case are obtained by matching the page-18 global errors to the general local/global correspondence. [PDF p. 5, anchor: paragraph following equation (3.3); PDF p. 18, anchor: two error-form statements]
hypotheses: The method is interpreted within the additive Runge-Kutta scheme (3.1): A,b multiply F, while A_eps,b_eps multiply F_eps at the same stage values. [PDF p. 4, anchor: equations (3.1a)-(3.1b)]

The approximation satisfies F_eps(y) - F(y) = O(epsilon) for any y, and tau is defined from F and F_eps. [PDF p. 3, anchor: equation (2.3); PDF p. 4, anchor: paragraph following equations (3.1a)-(3.1b)]

For the smooth conclusion, tau is well-behaved; inherited context describes this via existing bounded derivatives of F and F_eps and bounded derivatives of tau, permitting cancellation of corresponding perturbation terms. [PDF p. 6, anchor: standard regularity scenario; PDF p. 8, anchor: opening paragraph of Section 3.1.2]

For the nonsmooth conclusion, tau is not well-behaved; chopping is the motivating case in which F_eps and tau are not Lipschitz and derivatives of tau may fail to exist. [PDF p. 6, anchor: chopping discussion; PDF p. 18, anchor: nonsmooth error statement]

Stability is an inherited assumption for interpreting the page-18 quantity Error as a global error estimate. [PDF p. 2, anchor: Introduction stability limitation; PDF p. 5, anchor: local-to-global error paragraph]
conclusions: Method 4s3pC is presented as satisfying the simplified well-behaved-tau perturbation conditions through order m = 3 together with third-order consistency. [PDF p. 17, anchor: Section 4.3 opening paragraph; PDF p. 18, anchor: smooth error statement]
Explicit smooth-case claim: Error = O(Delta t^3) + O(epsilon Delta t^3). [PDF p. 18, anchor: first error-form statement following the coefficients]
Explicit nonsmooth-case claim: Error = O(Delta t^3) + O(epsilon Delta t^2). [PDF p. 18, anchor: second error-form statement following the coefficients]

Inherited one-step forms are E = O(Delta t^4) + O(epsilon Delta t^4) in the smooth case and E = O(Delta t^4) + O(epsilon Delta t^3) in the nonsmooth case; these are inferred from the general one-step/global relation and are not restated beside Method 4s3pC. [PDF p. 5, anchor: paragraph following equation (3.3); PDF p. 18, anchor: Method 4s3pC error statements]
definitions_and_conventions: Explicit combined-coefficient definitions are tilde_A=A+A_eps and tilde_b=b+b_eps; the paper also uses tilde_c=c+c_eps. [PDF p. 5, anchor: text following equations (3.2a)-(3.2b); PDF p. 11, anchor: arrays following equation (4.1c)]

The standard Butcher interpretation is e=(1,1,1,1)^T, c=Ae, c_eps=A_eps e, and tilde_c=tilde_A e=c+c_eps; c=Ae and the meaning of e are inherited conventions rather than explicit definitions in the selected passage. [PDF p. 2, anchor: equation (1.1); PDF p. 7, anchor: consistency-order list; PDF p. 11, anchor: arrays following equation (4.1c)]

The centered dot in expressions such as tilde_c dot tilde_c denotes componentwise vector multiplication under the standard B-series convention; the selected pages do not formally define that notation. [PDF p. 5, anchor: B-series coefficient table; PDF p. 7, anchor: third-order consistency conditions]
implicit_context: The underlying problem is an ODE u_t=F(u), but the state-space dimension and domain/codomain of F are not specified in the selected result. [PDF p. 1, anchor: opening ODE in the Introduction]

The page-18 symbol Error inherits the paper's convention for accumulated/global error, while E denotes one-step error. [PDF p. 5, anchor: paragraph following equation (3.3); PDF p. 18, anchor: Method 4s3pC error statements]

The four-stage and zero-filled-tableau interpretations are conventional readings of the coefficient display, not fully spelled-out matrices on page 18. [PDF p. 18, anchor: Method 4s3pC coefficient displays]

Section 4.3 presents the method as applicable beyond literal mixed floating-point evaluation: Figure 6 also uses different spatial discretizations for F and F_eps when their difference is well-behaved. [PDF p. 18, anchor: Figure 6 caption; PDF p. 19, anchor: Figure 6 discussion]
statement.algorithm_linkage: Method 4s3pC is the additive Runge-Kutta variant of equations (3.1a)-(3.1b) using the page-18 A,A_eps,b,b_eps data. Because b_eps is zero, the final update is weighted only through evaluations of F, while F_eps contributes through the stages via A_eps; this linkage is obtained by inserting the displayed coefficients into the general scheme. [PDF p. 4, anchor: equations (3.1a)-(3.1b); PDF p. 18, anchor: Method 4s3pC coefficient displays]
numerical_model: The abstract perturbation model is F_eps(y)-F(y)=O(epsilon) for any y, with tau(u)=(F(u)-F_eps(u))/epsilon. [PDF p. 3, anchor: equation (2.3); PDF p. 4, anchor: paragraph following equations (3.1a)-(3.1b)]

For mixed precision emulation, the paper uses chopping and gives order-of-magnitude examples epsilon approximately 10^-8 for single precision and epsilon approximately 10^-4 for half precision. [PDF p. 4, anchor: first paragraph and numerical setup]
The analysis treats epsilon as a single constant upper bound rather than a stage-dependent or operation-dependent rounding parameter. [PDF p. 20, anchor: final paragraph of Conclusions]
No IEEE rounding mode, unit-roundoff formula, accumulation model, or per-operation relative-error model is specified. [PDF p. 4, anchor: truncation description; PDF p. 6, anchor: chopping discussion]
error_notions: E_sch is the one-step approximation error of the underlying scheme and E_per is the one-step perturbation error; E=E_sch+E_per. [PDF p. 5, anchor: paragraph following equation (3.3)]
Under stability, reducing a one-step term O(Delta t^(p+1))+O(epsilon Delta t^(m+1)) gives the global form O(Delta t^p)+O(epsilon Delta t^m). [PDF p. 5, anchor: local-to-global error paragraph]
The selected result states asymptotic forward/global error orders, not backward error, residual error, or a componentwise error guarantee. [PDF p. 18, anchor: Method 4s3pC error statements]
norms: No norm is specified for E, Error, F_eps-F, or the constants hidden by O notation. [PDF p. 4, anchor: F_eps approximation paragraph; PDF p. 5, anchor: local/global error paragraph; PDF p. 18, anchor: Method 4s3pC error statements]

Products such as b c and b A c are algebraic row-vector/matrix/column-vector products; products inside parentheses such as c dot c are componentwise products under inherited Runge-Kutta B-series notation. [PDF p. 5, anchor: B-series tables; PDF p. 7, anchor: consistency conditions]
constants_and_indexing: Third-order consistency preserves all lower-order requirements: tilde_b e=1; tilde_b tilde_c=1/2; tilde_b(tilde_c dot tilde_c)=1/3; and tilde_b tilde_A tilde_c=1/6. [PDF p. 7, anchor: consistency-order list]
For m>=1, equation (3.5a) requires, under its n>=1 label, b_eps e=0. [PDF p. 8, anchor: equation (3.5a)]
For m>=2, equations (3.5b)-(3.5c) additionally require: under n>=1, b_eps tilde_c=0 and tilde_b c_eps=0; under n>=2, b_eps c_eps=0. [PDF p. 8, anchor: equations (3.5b)-(3.5c)]

For m>=3 and n>=1, equation (3.5d) additionally requires b_eps tilde_A tilde_c=0, tilde_b A_eps tilde_c=0, tilde_b tilde_A c_eps=0, b_eps(tilde_c dot tilde_c)=0, and tilde_b(tilde_c dot c_eps)=0. [PDF p. 8, anchor: equation (3.5d)]

For m>=3 and n>=2, equation (3.5e) additionally requires b_eps A_eps tilde_c=0, b_eps tilde_A c_eps=0, tilde_b A_eps c_eps=0, b_eps(c_eps dot tilde_c)=0, and tilde_b(c_eps dot c_eps)=0. [PDF p. 8, anchor: equation (3.5e)]
For m>=3 and n>=3, equation (3.5f) additionally requires b_eps A_eps c_eps=0 and b_eps(c_eps dot c_eps)=0. [PDF p. 8, anchor: equation (3.5f)]

Coefficient subscripts are one-based stage indices. The displayed decimal coefficients carry fifteen digits after the decimal point, except the exact-looking entry a_eps_41=-2. [PDF p. 18, anchor: Method 4s3pC coefficient displays]
higher_order_terms: The claimed smooth global error retains two separate asymptotic contributions, O(Delta t^3) and O(epsilon Delta t^3); neither may be dropped or merged without an additional relation between epsilon and Delta t. [PDF p. 18, anchor: smooth error statement]
The claimed nonsmooth global error retains O(Delta t^3) and O(epsilon Delta t^2). [PDF p. 18, anchor: nonsmooth error statement]
The perturbation table is expanded only through third order in Delta t and third order in epsilon; terms beyond that truncation are not enumerated. [PDF p. 6, anchor: perturbation expansion table]

No big-O constants, uniformity range, limiting path for epsilon versus Delta t, or threshold at which one contribution dominates is specified in the Method 4s3pC statement. [PDF p. 18, anchor: two Method 4s3pC error statements]
exceptional_values: The source does not model NaNs, infinities, overflow, underflow, subnormals, or exceptional solver failure; chopping is represented only as a bounded, non-Lipschitz operator. [PDF p. 6, anchor: chopping discussion]

In the smooth case, derivative existence and boundedness exclude the derivative failures discussed for chopping, but the paper gives no precise domain or uniform boundedness quantifiers. [PDF p. 6, anchor: two regularity scenarios]

undebatable_constraints: The source claim must retain all four consistency equalities through p=3, not merely the two third-order equalities. [PDF p. 7, anchor: consistency-order list]

The source claim must retain every condition in (3.5a)-(3.5f) when asserting smooth perturbation order m=3, including the conditions grouped under n>=1, n>=2, and n>=3. [PDF p. 8, anchor: equations (3.5a)-(3.5f)]
A and b belong to the F evaluations, while A_eps and b_eps belong to F_eps; swapping these roles changes the algorithm. [PDF p. 4, anchor: equations (3.1a)-(3.1b)]

The Method 4s3pC coefficient values and signs must be preserved exactly as printed, including a_eps_41=-2, a_43=-1.895660952342050, the negative fourth weight, and b_eps=(0,0,0,0). [PDF p. 18, anchor: Method 4s3pC coefficient displays]

Both regularity branches are part of the result: smooth tau gives O(Delta t^3)+O(epsilon Delta t^3), while non-well-behaved tau gives O(Delta t^3)+O(epsilon Delta t^2). [PDF p. 18, anchor: two error-form statements]
The global interpretation is conditional on stability inherited from the general framework. [PDF p. 2, anchor: stability limitation; PDF p. 5, anchor: local-to-global error paragraph]

The big-O statements must not be strengthened into explicit inequalities, exact equalities, norm-specific estimates, or bounds with specified constants. [PDF p. 5, anchor: local/global error paragraph; PDF p. 18, anchor: Method 4s3pC error statements]

ambiguities.issue: The printed decimal coefficients are not identified as exact values or rounded approximations. [PDF p. 18, anchor: Method 4s3pC coefficient displays]
ambiguities.evidence: The order conditions on pages 7-8 are exact zero and rational equalities, but page 18 supplies only finite decimal coefficients and no tolerance or generating exact values. Under the standard zero-fill and row-sum conventions, literal exact-decimal arithmetic does not satisfy every equality exactly; for example, 2(tilde_b tilde_c)-1 evaluates to -1511838180411276/10^30 from the printed numbers. [PDF p. 7, anchor: consistency conditions; PDF p. 18, anchor: coefficient displays]
ambiguities.impact: A formal contract cannot silently treat both the printed decimals as exact rationals and all order conditions as exact facts. It must either retain unknown exact coefficients represented approximately by the display, introduce numerical tolerances, or record that the literal-decimal theorem is false. [PDF p. 7, anchor: exact consistency equalities; PDF p. 18, anchor: decimal coefficient display]

ambiguities.issue: Page 18 does not print complete 4-by-4 matrices. [PDF p. 18, anchor: Method 4s3pC coefficient displays]
ambiguities.evidence: Only lower-triangular entries are listed; all upper-triangular entries and the diagonal of A are omitted. Standard Butcher-tableau practice suggests they are zero, but the passage does not state that convention. [PDF p. 18, anchor: Method 4s3pC coefficient displays]
ambiguities.impact: Reconstructing explicit matrices requires a zero-fill assumption that should be marked as inherited rather than quoted as an explicit source assertion. [PDF p. 18, anchor: Method 4s3pC coefficient displays]

ambiguities.issue: The sign convention for tau is internally inconsistent. [PDF p. 3, anchor: equation (2.3); PDF p. 5, anchor: equations (3.2a)-(3.2b)]
ambiguities.evidence: Equation (2.3) defines tau=(F-F_eps)/epsilon, while substituting that identity into equations (3.1a)-(3.1b) would produce negative epsilon A_eps tau and epsilon b_eps tau terms; equations (3.2a)-(3.2b) print those terms with positive signs. [PDF p. 3, anchor: equation (2.3); PDF p. 4, anchor: equations (3.1a)-(3.1b); PDF p. 5, anchor: equations (3.2a)-(3.2b)]
ambiguities.impact: A formalized recurrence must choose a sign convention. The zero-valued cancellation conditions and asymptotic orders are sign-insensitive, but an exact equivalence between the two algorithm forms is not. [PDF p. 5, anchor: equations (3.2a)-(3.2b); PDF p. 8, anchor: zero-valued conditions (3.5)]

ambiguities.issue: The notation e, c, c_eps, componentwise dot, and the labels n>=1, n>=2, n>=3 are not formally introduced in the selected condition list. [PDF p. 7, anchor: consistency conditions; PDF p. 8, anchor: equations (3.5a)-(3.5f)]
ambiguities.evidence: A later worked tableau explicitly gives tilde_c=c+c_eps, and the perturbation table associates successive epsilon powers with the grouped conditions, but no nearby sentence declares e as the ones vector, c=Ae, c_eps=A_eps e, or n as the epsilon-power count. [PDF p. 6, anchor: perturbation expansion table; PDF p. 8, anchor: equations (3.5); PDF p. 11, anchor: arrays following equation (4.1c)]

ambiguities.issue: Well-behaved is descriptive rather than a fully quantified analytic hypothesis. [PDF p. 6, anchor: regularity scenarios; PDF p. 8, anchor: opening of Section 3.1.2]
ambiguities.evidence: The paper says that F and F_eps have existing bounded derivatives and that tau and its derivatives are bounded, but it does not specify derivative order, domain, norm, or uniformity in epsilon. [PDF p. 6, anchor: standard regularity scenario]
ambiguities.impact: The smooth error claim cannot be translated into a unique formal analytic theorem without adding choices that the source does not settle. [PDF p. 18, anchor: smooth Method 4s3pC error statement]

ambiguities.issue: The scope of the nonsmooth error statement is not fully specified. [PDF p. 17, anchor: Section 4.3 opening; PDF p. 18, anchor: nonsmooth error statement]

The sentence is grammatically missing an explicit 'when' before 'tau is not well-behaved.' [PDF p. 17, anchor: Section 4.3 opening paragraph; PDF p. 18, anchor: second error-form statement]
ambiguities.impact: The safest contract preserves the nonsmooth asymptotic form as an explicit paper claim but does not strengthen it into a theorem for every bounded non-Lipschitz perturbation. [PDF p. 18, anchor: nonsmooth error statement]

ambiguities.issue: The error norm and asymptotic limiting regime are omitted. [PDF p. 18, anchor: Method 4s3pC error statements]
ambiguities.evidence: The paper writes only Error and big-O expressions; it supplies no norm, constants, quantifier order, or rule for whether epsilon is fixed as Delta t tends to zero. [PDF p. 5, anchor: local/global error paragraph; PDF p. 18, anchor: two error-form statements]
ambiguities.impact: A formal statement should retain abstract error predicates or add explicitly documented modeling assumptions rather than selecting a norm or epsilon-Delta t limit silently. [PDF p. 18, anchor: Method 4s3pC error statements]

contract_plain_english: Method 4s3pC is a four-stage reading of the additive Runge-Kutta framework in which the printed A,b coefficients multiply F, the printed A_eps,b_eps coefficients multiply F_eps, and b_eps is zero. [PDF p. 4, anchor: equations (3.1a)-(3.1b); PDF p. 18, anchor: Method 4s3pC coefficient displays] The paper presents it as third-order consistent and as satisfying every simplified smooth-perturbation condition through m=3. [PDF p. 7, anchor: consistency conditions; PDF p. 8, anchor: equations (3.5a)-(3.5f); PDF p. 17, anchor: Section 4.3 opening paragraph] Subject to the paper's inherited stability requirement, it claims global error O(Delta t^3)+O(epsilon Delta t^3) when tau is well-behaved and O(Delta t^3)+O(epsilon Delta t^2) when tau is not well-behaved. [PDF p. 5, anchor: local-to-global error paragraph; PDF p. 18, anchor: two error-form statements] The source does not settle whether the displayed decimals are exact, whether omitted tableau entries are zero by definition, the exact analytic meaning of well-behaved, the error norm, or the epsilon-versus-Delta t limiting regime; these omissions must not be resolved silently. [PDF p. 6, anchor: regularity discussion; PDF p. 18, anchor: coefficient and error displays]
